title: Inspect Annals installation and maintenance
summary: Read release selection, dedicated decisions provisioning, deployment admission, scheduler ownership, program recovery guarantees.
use_when: Annals installed state, release selection, maintenance, deployment recovery, scheduler ownership, or platform limits must be understood.
do_not_use_when: The actual task is ordinary source retention, interpretation, corpus administration, or inbox operation.
An operation requires unsupported direct state editing, storage cleanup, a foreign schedule takeover, or unapproved destructive replacement.
outcome: Completion of the selected placement and setup instructions, or the separately documented explicit manual installation, maintenance or recovery result. Deployment completion does not establish application health.
effects: The schema-2 annals-install deploy command places the release, creates or migrates the primary, decisions and registered libraries in place, writes configuration, and selects the two inbox schedules without application holds or durable-work draining. It suspends owned schedules and waits for their active processes before runtime publication.
The maintenance, ownership-proof and compensation procedures for explicitly invoked `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` and `migrate-to-user` do not run from schema-2 `deploy`.
Stages and atomically selects a complete immutable release containing Annals, Annals Usage, runners, configuration, and provider documentation.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Registers an immutable Clockwork definition for `annals/inbox`. Before disabling or replacing a prior selection, verifies that its digest resolves to the complete current Annals release definition. Establishes maintenance, migrates the library, and atomically switches the binding after the release is ready.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: During legacy system migration, the child deployer returns an inert rendered definition under maintenance; the outer migration durably commits the permanent user-state root before it registers or selects that definition.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Removes or restores a legacy LaunchDaemon or LaunchAgent only when its complete plist, owner, and mode match the exact Annals rendering; migration also proves the system service absent before removing its files or clearing maintenance, and additional launchd keys are foreign.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: The decisions provisioner creates the separate database with its immutable decisions role. Existing state must retain that role after the supported schema check. It owns only that database's bound spool, config, logs, and `annals/decisions-inbox` definition. It shares the Annals update lock and never changes `annals/inbox`.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Before opening decisions state or selecting its schedule, the provisioner checks existing mutable control files and both fixed logs. They must be operator-owned private regular files with one hard link. It creates absent logs privately and rejects symbolic or hard-linked targets.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: With `--keep-maintenance`, records and retains an Annals-owned decisions maintenance hold for an outer cutover; a later successful invocation clears only that matching owned hold.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: A failed pre-commit cutover restores compatible program, configuration and schedule state while retaining current library and spool data.

The Cell manifest command performs file placement, configuration, initialization or migration, and schedule selection. It does not acquire application maintenance, drain durable work, check readiness, or recover automatically. It suspends owned schedules and waits for their active processes before runtime publication, then restores saved enabled intent with the new definitions. Actual state mutations retain their native locks. Explicit manual maintenance and recovery commands remain separate.

Program publication copies the selected release into fixed regular files beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Annals/install/runtime. Public commands use that runtime tree; current and previous retain immutable UUID archive selections. Code signing and runtime path identity are separate from release identity. New Clockwork definitions use schema 3: they retain the archive release ID, root and exact hashes, and execute the fixed runtime image. Publication precedes registration. Before publication, deployment runs the disable transition for owned Clockwork bindings and waits for their active processes, including an active manual run on a disabled binding. It restores saved enabled intent after registration; a failed instruction can leave the owned bindings disabled. Existing history, delivery records, enabled intent and incident halts retain their meaning. Retained definitions and wrapper bytes from before this change keep their legacy execution paths until a new installation or definition selects the runtime image.

Manual primary installation requires annals/decisions-inbox disabled because its separate provisioner owns the schedule handoff. With --no-start, annals/inbox must also be disabled. The installer rejects enabled bindings without a handoff and waits for active processes in retained disabled bindings before runtime publication. A later explicit schedule handoff selects the matching definition.
authority: Annals owns its installed programs, library, spool, schedule requirements, configuration, migration, maintenance, domain result, and recovery.

Clockwork owns the immutable executable definitions, selected bindings, non-overlap enforcement, launchd projections, and activation process history for `annals/inbox` and `annals/decisions-inbox`; it never owns Annals job or corpus success.
Nucleus remains separately authoritative for Codex execution and authentication and is not stopped or replaced by an Annals deployment.
success: The manifest command completes the declared placement and setup instructions. An omitted enabled setting preserves captured schedule intent; a new schedule defaults enabled. Existing data, operator pauses, application maintenance, and incident halts remain in place. Completion does not establish application health.
failure_and_recovery: Product-owned schema-three schedule definitions select halt-until-approved. The first abnormal attempt ends the current run. Clockwork permits later activations before the shared service-health threshold. By default, five consecutive failed read-only checks, at least 60 seconds apart, establish the halt and alert eligibility together. Healthy or inactive checks, including operator pause, clear a pending failure episode. Established halts require exact binding resume approval; definition switches, deployment and product resume/retry preserve them. Product domain state and explicit retries remain product-owned.

The manifest command does not inspect installed maintenance support or perform automatic recovery. An interrupted command leaves completed effects in place; inspect the retained command log and use explicit product procedures when needed.

After an interrupted schema-2 deploy command, inspect its retained log and current selections before further instructions; completed effects remain in place. For a retained explicit manual transaction, use `annals-install recover` without deleting its maintenance or editing spool receipts.

The schema-2 deploy command does not probe storage readiness. Actual staging, migration or publication writes can fail for insufficient space. Separately invoked diagnostics can report `storage_probe_failed`.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: A failed ordinary update preserves current data and restores compatible program and control state before work resumes.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Before child installation begins, a legacy migration failure can restore the system installation without registering a definition. Phase installing, or rewritten with child evidence, retains moved state and outer and child recovery evidence. A committed interruption or unproved system-service retirement retains maintenance and its handoff for idempotent completion.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: A decisions provisioning failure before binding commit preserves current database state and restores compatible program, config and exact attributable prior schedule state. Unprovable compatibility or restoration keeps maintenance and transaction evidence.
The installer supplies no data backup, data restore, or reset mode. Existing data backup artifacts are unchanged.
privacy: Installed library, spool, configuration, logs, and Nucleus output may contain complete private sources and model context.
Deployment must preserve private user ownership and permissions for current data and existing prior data artifacts.
does_not_authorize: Running `products/annals/release.sh`, which commits, tags, and pushes.
Resetting an existing library or spool.
Clearing user data as storage remediation, or lowering or disabling the inbox storage reserve, without the user's explicit consent for the exact target and scope.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Disabling a same-key Clockwork binding or removing a same-label plist or installed pathname without proving its exact Annals release or rendered-file identity.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Concurrent same-user direct Clockwork mutation of `annals/inbox` during deployment or migration; ownership inspection and binding mutation are not a compare-and-swap, and a detected change fails closed behind the maintenance recovery gate.
Using decisions-library authority to mutate the primary `annals/inbox` binding, the primary library or spool, Nucleus, release bytes, or a foreign `annals/decisions-inbox` definition.
Deleting prior generations, logs, or retained failed envelopes.

consumers.statement: Local operators and deployment coordinators may inspect or rely on Annals release selection, owned admission holds, supported installation and recovery guarantees, or platform boundaries. Performing a cutover follows annals.install.operate.
This operation is not source development, Git publication, routine library administration, library reset, or storage cleanup.

preconditions.statement: The schema-2 `annals-install deploy` command takes the declared candidate and source paths plus optional boolean enabled settings. It does not inspect installed maintenance support, hold or drain durable work, check readiness or recover automatically. It suspends owned schedules and waits for their active processes before runtime publication.

For explicit `annals-install install`, select the binaries and provider bundles and supply absolute candidate, Nucleus socket and Clockwork paths. Writes require enough physical capacity. CI validation is separate from installer command completion.

Explicit `annals-install install` compares the selected `annals/inbox` definition with the current release. Explicit `migrate-to-user` requires an absent or disabled binding without a selected digest before commit. Schema-2 `deploy` reads enabled intent and selects its new definition directly.

Explicit `annals-install provision-decisions` takes the currently selected retained Cell release and checks the selected prior decisions definition against its dedicated state and recorded release. Schema-2 `deploy` creates or migrates decisions state and selects its new definition directly.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Existing decisions config, database sidecars, spool controls and identity files, maintenance and logs require private operator ownership and one hard link. The library retains its immutable decisions role.

Prompt preparation requires initialized private Bazaar state and a complete cell.prompts.annals selection. The default database is ~/.local/share/bazaar/bazaar.sqlite3; callers accept an absolute CELL_BAZAAR_DATABASE override. Reads fail without creating state or using embedded fallback text.

Manual primary installation requires annals/decisions-inbox disabled because its separate provisioner owns the schedule handoff. With --no-start, annals/inbox must also be disabled. The installer rejects enabled bindings without a handoff and waits for active processes in retained disabled bindings before runtime publication. A later explicit schedule handoff selects the matching definition.

inputs.statement: Maintenance accepts the selected library path and one run ID of 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, or periods, without a leading period. A controlled installer command may set CELL_DEPLOYMENT_RUN_ID; existing holds require that exact sole owner and exclusive drained admission, while absent holds use ordinary admission.

Explicit `annals-install install` accepts absolute binary, provider, Nucleus socket and Clockwork paths. Explicit `provision-decisions` takes a retained release root, socket, Clockwork path and optional --keep-maintenance. Schema-2 `deploy` takes candidate/source paths and settings on stdin.
The deployer does not accept release publication, arbitrary cleanup, manual receipt editing, implicit data deletion, or Nucleus replacement as installation inputs.

outputs.statement: Maintenance returns the standard ok/data envelope with protocol_version 1, contract_version 1, holds, and drained without opening or initializing SQLite. Drained describes participating live command admission and is not by itself proof that durable work or Nucleus jobs are terminal.

Schema-2 `deploy` completes release placement, configuration, library initialization or migration, and direct schedule selection. The release contains both payloads, the installer, frontend/runner roles and provider bundles. It does not verify native signatures, execute --version or --help, or establish runtime readiness. The explicit manual routines retain their configuration, private-state ownership and transaction guards.

Explicit `annals-install provision-decisions` returns a body-free ok/data envelope with config path, library ID, Clockwork key and digest, selected/enabled state, maintenance and release ID. Schema-2 `deploy` returns command completion and release ID; the executor uses its exit code.
Separately invoked operator diagnostics expose versions, Nucleus health, Annals statistics, inbox status and Annals Usage diagnosis. These observations are not schema-2 deployment gates.

data_semantics.statement: Named library registration and runtime readiness are separate. Existing primary and decisions operator paths are not automatically adopted as catalog names, and creating a named library adds no schedule.
An ordinary update migrates and preserves the active library and spool. Unsupported schemas stop deployment without resetting current data.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Maintenance is distinct from operator pause and the storage gate; these manual routines clear only their own maintenance after commit. Schema-2 deploy leaves existing maintenance in place.

A closed storage gate does not itself reject release placement. Schema-2 deploy runs no storage-readiness probe; actual writes can fail if physical capacity is insufficient. Explicit diagnostics can separately report probe failures.

identity_and_units.statement: Product versions, provider releases, immutable release identity, current selector, Clockwork keys `annals/inbox` and `annals/decisions-inbox`, immutable definition digests, persistent decisions library ID, library schema, and library and spool identities are distinct identities.
Separately invoked storage checks and reserve comparisons use filesystem bytes. Runtime freshness and service checks are point-in-time diagnostics, not schema-2 deployment evidence.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: The schema-2 command publishes the staged release after its requested configuration and library setup instructions complete. It does not gate publication on service checks. Explicit manual install and recovery follow their transaction commit rules.
Installation completion reflects setup and publication. Runtime diagnostics are separate observations and are not installation gates.
No deployment-duration, service-availability, rollback-retention duration, or disk-capacity service-level objective is promised.

access.statement: Initialization, migration, and recovery leave readable persistent WAL coordination files for readers without write access. Named creation prepares them at the final library path. Migration prepares the configured spool control lock. Maintenance status opens existing private locks read-only and never creates or repairs a gate. Missing required coordination state stops inspection until an authorized setup or recovery operation prepares it.

The supported boundary is the repository-owned macOS deployers operating the current user's private primary installation or physically separate decisions state and only their respective Clockwork keys.
The operation does not own or replace Nucleus, publish Git state, delete recovery material, or grant direct library and spool editing.

The separately documented Linux route uses packaged systemd service/timer files and explicit service-account configuration; macOS transactional selector/rollback guarantees do not apply to that route.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Product-owned schema-three schedule definitions select halt-until-approved. The first abnormal attempt ends the current run. Clockwork permits later activations before the shared service-health threshold. By default, five consecutive failed read-only checks, at least 60 seconds apart, establish the halt and alert eligibility together. Healthy or inactive checks, including operator pause, clear a pending failure episode. Established halts require exact binding resume approval; definition switches, deployment and product resume/retry preserve them. Product domain state and explicit retries remain product-owned.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: The primary deployer discovers registered catalog libraries, records their identity and paths, fences command admission, drains admitted work, and performs transactional schema migrations in place. Program recovery preserves all current library data and instruction history. It does not restore earlier data.

The durable per-library gate is the private sibling <database>.cell-maintenance. Hold atomically prevents new mutations, admitted commands may settle, and repeated holds or releases are idempotent. Release removes only the named owner and preserves operator pause. Corpus and decision-feed reads plus inbox pause and interrupt remain available; public CLI client mutations share the same fence before database access.

The manifest command completes the declared placement and setup instructions. An omitted enabled setting preserves captured schedule intent; a new schedule defaults enabled. Existing data, operator pauses, application maintenance, and incident halts remain in place. Completion does not establish application health.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Deployment stages and registers an inactive exact-release definition, then establishes maintenance. It verifies and disables only an exact current-release Clockwork selection and stops any owned legacy LaunchAgent. It captures recovery state, migrates the current library, switches selectors and one Clockwork binding, verifies the result, then clears maintenance.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: The former-system migration is the exception to pre-commit definition registration: its child renders an inert definition under maintenance, and the outer migration durably records the target state as permanent before registering and selecting it. RunAtLoad remains maintenance-gated until the system service is proved absent and exact legacy retirement completes. System-state rollback is limited to failure before child installation begins. Phase installing, or rewritten with child evidence, retains the moved state and outer and child recovery evidence instead of moving state back.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Rollback restores the exact prior definition only when that binding was enabled, or restores the prior owned legacy LaunchAgent, never both. A previously absent or disabled binding remains disabled without transient activation; its inactive selected digest may remain the candidate digest. If exclusive restoration cannot be proved, Annals leaves unproved scheduler state untouched, keeps maintenance, removes its public selectors, and retains private recovery material.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: An ordinary pre-commit failure preserves current library and spool data. Program rollback requires compatibility with the retained data before admission resumes.
Credentials remain forward-only. The installer has no data reset or data restore route.

For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Decisions provisioning prepares absent state under maintenance, registers an inactive definition, drains owned work, migrates existing state transactionally in place, and selects annals/decisions-inbox. It clears only its own gate unless --keep-maintenance was requested.
Explicit `annals-install provision-decisions` changes only decisions state and its binding; the primary library and binding remain separate. All installer writes serialize on the Annals update lock.

Callers resolve cell.prompts.annals to exact component versions before preparing new work. Prompt edits affect new selections. Retained requests, packet inputs, library revisions, and assignment snapshots preserve their existing recovery and retention semantics.

Program publication copies the selected release into fixed regular files beneath ~/Library/Application Support/Annals/install/runtime. Public commands use that runtime tree; current and previous retain immutable UUID archive selections. Code signing and runtime path identity are separate from release identity. New Clockwork definitions use schema 3: they retain the archive release ID, root and exact hashes, and execute the fixed runtime image. Publication precedes registration. Before publication, deployment runs the disable transition for owned Clockwork bindings and waits for their active processes, including an active manual run on a disabled binding. It restores saved enabled intent after registration; a failed instruction can leave the owned bindings disabled. Existing history, delivery records, enabled intent and incident halts retain their meaning. Retained definitions and wrapper bytes from before this change keep their legacy execution paths until a new installation or definition selects the runtime image.

operational_limits.statement: The supported deployers are per-user macOS Clockwork installations, require absolute inputs, serialize on one Annals update lock, stage one complete generation, and need enough physical capacity for release, migration, and rollback artifacts.
The installer provides no library reset, data backup, or data restore. Deployment authority never implies data cleanup, reserve reduction, prior-generation deletion, or service work outside Annals.
No maximum installed-state size, deployment time, retained-generation count, or service downtime bound is promised here.
Data backup and data restoration are not supplied. Existing backup files are left unchanged.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: For explicit `annals-install install`, `provision-decisions`, `recover` or `migrate-to-user`: Supported library migration and retained legacy instruction provenance are defined by annals.libraries. Program rollback requires compatibility with every current library. An incompatible prior program leaves maintenance and transaction evidence retained.

Annals Usage doctor may prove readiness under the same sole Nucleus deployment hold through the typed health_for_deployment interface, including runtime drain, authentication, and harness readiness; it does not turn held public Nucleus admission into normal job admission.

Package versions, provider releases, library schema, Nucleus protocol and release IDs have separate meanings. Schema-2 deploy records declared paths and performs setup without a compatibility or readiness audit.
Library changes use only supported migrations; provider selectors follow the same release generation as their executables for rollback.
No cross-release installation support window, migration horizon, or deprecation period is promised.

Selection version 1 preserves the migration baseline for historical execution. Changed tool descriptions use new immutable Nucleus toolset identities; permission policy and structural schemas remain caller-owned.

reliances.statement: Deployment records the supplied Nucleus paths and socket without checking authentication, compatibility, or runtime readiness. It does not stop or replace Nucleus.

Schedule setup and unattended inbox processing rely on the declared Clockwork schedule contract for definition registration, one selected binding, non-overlap, activation history and launchd projection.
Annals promises no launchd availability or wake-up latency beyond the observations exposed by Clockwork.

Bazaar owns shared selection format, exact component loading, rendering, and trusted description expansion. Annals chooses its component set and owns authored meaning, runtime inputs, typed request and toolset assembly, permissions, execution, domain effects, and recovery. Prepared text grants no additional authority.
The packaged Linux route relies on systemd activation and Linux service-account/filesystem administration without a dedicated installed contract.
